The function \(x\log x\) is strictly decreasing there; equality of all normalized weights implies common additive scalar offsets, which cannot have nonzero sign under the sum-one constraint, proving injectivity. For \(n=3\), the exact invariant line P(s) has return map F, with F(0)=sqrt(2)-1, F(1/3)=1/3, and log-odds derivative g. The explicit exact inequalities \(g(1/3)<0<g(\sqrt2-1)\), strict g monotonicity, and IVT give two distinct points inside the first image with the same nonuniform output throughout an open interval; the original preimages exist by IVT again. The standalone script checks one illustrative collision but is not the proof. Critical inequalities and quantifiers were recomputed independently.

value.rationale: The source naturally poses a question about the finite-time information loss of a globally contracting normalization map: does it continue erasing distinct initial states after its first boundary-regularizing step? The theorem gives a sharp two-sided dimension threshold, an entire open interval of exact nonuniform second-step collision targets in dimension three, and a no-later-collisions rigidity theorem for all higher dimensions. The three-dimensional fold requires a delicate strict endpoint inequality (\(9801>9800\)) and is not merely another proof of global convergence or a trivial one-step fiber substitution. It is a precise, structurally motivated extension rather than a routine finite table.
